title: LoginStage::Asserting holds no task; the ceremony lives in the UI's CeremonyUi and cancel/failure never leave the stage
trigger: Log in using passkey, open the OS ceremony, press Cancel/Esc (close_passkey_ceremony) or let it fail (CeremonyEvent::Failed): the box closes and a note shows, but login.stage stays Asserting
effect: Nothing visible today: is_waiting() is false and the next begin_login reuses fresh options or fetches again; the stage is a stale in-flight value until then
fix: Leave Asserting from the ceremony's own end (cancel/fail -> Idle/Failed) or hold the ceremony worker in the stage

title: RemoveStage::Removing is the only passkey stage that after_passkeys_ingest never drops when its request is lost
trigger: Passkeys list: delete a passkey, the connection drops before removeLoginPasskey is answered (request leaves session.requests with no answer or error)
effect: is_removing() stays true so remove_passkey returns InvalidRequest for every passkey and the delete row shows busy until the session is rebuilt; FetchingOptions, Sending, the list and the login stages all have a drop_lost arm
fix: Add PasskeysState::drop_lost_removal(pending) next to drop_lost_register and call it from after_passkeys_ingest, leaving Removing for Idle (and the list Stale)

title: LimitState::Asked(request) is never left when the request is lost without an answer, and should_ask() treats any entry as asked
trigger: Open a chat action that hits a Premium limit (ensure_premium_limit sends getPremiumLimit), the connection drops before the answer; the request leaves session.requests with no answer or error
effect: The limit box and toast for that kind keep the built-in fallback numbers until the Premium explainer is fetched (premium info then supplies the pair); the live pair is never asked again this session
fix: Add LimitStore::drop_lost(pending) that removes Asked(id) entries whose request is gone, called from the same after-ingest hook as the passkey drop_lost arms
